provenance.why: For any reaction time: an action is held until the next one starts, so every action must be safe to hold for a second or more. A random code may hold a turn and spin the player round; walking forward and firing does not.

provenance.why: For a slow player: an order outlives its goal when the next decision is a second away, and a player told to stand and fire at an enemy already dead stands still while the next one shoots. The rule says what to do once its focus is gone: walk on toward the goal, firing.

provenance.why: general rewrite of the v2 tree
In real time the helper turns toward the focus every tic, so the skill needs no turning rules: it faces the focus, then does the caller's action.

focus.question: Which visible enemy has the greatest shown width in pixels?

provenance.why: At 70 health, five firing decisions had missed the 8-pixel-wide focus while a 15-pixel-wide enemy remained available; continued unsuccessful firing ended in death. Selecting the wider target earlier improves the chance of eliminating a threat before the action delay and incoming damage exhaust the remaining health.
